A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, title, workflow, and principal experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on two DST variants, MO-HalfCheetah, and MO-Hopper, including embedding comparisons, an MLP ablation, and qualitative policy analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds LSTM encoder evaluations and neighborhood-size sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The proposed trajectory-extraction, transformer-encoding, mean-aggregation, and diagnostic workflow is unchanged, including its losses and policy-ordering procedure. The LSTM is introduced as an ablation comparator, not as a replacement component of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Smooth DST, Left–Right DST, two-objective MO-HalfCheetah, and three-objective MO-Hopper. The added experiments reuse this coverage. The expanded conflict-zone example is hypothetical, not an additional evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: v2 retains the manual DST embeddings and MLP comparator and adds an evaluated LSTM encoder across all four environments (Appendix C.4, Tables 7–8). This is a limited extension of the comparator set.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a neighborhood-size sweep for the existing 80-policy HalfCheetah and 160-policy Hopper sets. Table 4 revises max_len from 100 to 20 for DST and 100 for MuJoCo. This is a reported setting revision; the PDFs do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens validation of design choices by adding neighborhood-size sensitivity tests and a recurrent-encoder ablation with distance plots across all four environments. These test metric robustness and dependence on encoder architecture beyond v1's retained manual-embedding validation, MLP comparison, and policy case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report one MORL/D run, five encoder seeds, means and standard deviations, and individual-seed plots. The new LSTM results and sensitivity figures extend this reporting practice without introducing additional uncertainty procedures or establishing an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: The original scores in Tables 1, 2, 5, and 6 remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results on alternative encoder behavior and neighborhood sensitivity. For example, Table 8 reports LSTM HalfCheetah trustworthiness of 0.976 ± 0.005 and continuity of 0.982 ± 0.003. Figures 11–16 add sensitivity curves and LSTM distance patterns; these are new evaluations, not improvements to retained scores.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly asserts the admissibility bound k < (2N−1)/3 and explains large-k metric collapse through the denominator of Qk approaching zero. This adds limited mathematical reasoning; the original definitions, losses, diagnostic formulas, and absence of formal proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and central conclusion retain the same claims: a modular diagnostic workflow flags behavioral differences hidden by objective proximity for human inspection. The revision does not expand the claimed ability to determine deployment relevance or reward adequacy automatically.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the sensitivity curves as supporting local diagnostic stability and attributes extreme-k collapse to normalization. It also refines the encoder comparison: simpler encoders recover global neighborhood metrics, while the transformer is described as more reliable for DST distance structure. Existing stakeholder-preference and policy-ordering limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly discloses k=2, documents the LSTM's per-step MLP, two recurrent layers, padding handling, and output projection, and expands hyperparameter explanations in Appendix A.2. Table 4 also revises the trajectory-length setting. Hardware and code/data access information were already present in v1.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to MORL, behavioral representation learning, and reward specification are unchanged. The added reminder that encoders can be substituted reiterates the existing modularity claim.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 adds localized explanations, an expanded deployment illustration, and appendix subsections for sensitivity and LSTM evaluation. Publication information, author contact details, and the equal-contribution note are also added.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual evidence with two sensitivity figures, four multipanel LSTM figures, and two result tables. Original transformer seed figures are retained as Figures 17–20, and the policy-analysis table moves from Table 7 to Table 9. Existing displays also reflow around the additions and publication headers.

improvement.justification: The LSTM ablation and neighborhood-size sweep provide useful checks on design choices that v1 examined less fully. Explicit k=2 reporting and additional implementation details also aid reproducibility. These strengthen supporting validation while preserving the main results and contribution. Incomplete labeling of the compared spaces in the new LSTM tables limits interpretation, so the overall gain is modest.
